process_area.title: Global Sourcing Strategy, Source-Market & Sourcing-Model Design

value_stream.name: Global Sourcing, Import Buying & Sourcing Agent Management

fields.Participants: Global Sourcing, Merchandising/Buyers (links to VS-01/VS-19), Supply Planning (links to VS-02), Vendor Mgmt (links to VS-03), Quality (links to VS-31), Finance (links to VS-17.4/VS-106), Compliance (links to VS-87/VS-22), Strategy (links to VS-33)
fields.Trigger: Annual merchandise/financial plan (links to VS-101); category strategy cycle

workflows.name: Global Sourcing Strategy & Import Category Sourcing Plan

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "countries, and the make/buy/consolidation approach, aligned to the merchandise…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-import of "import business case per category" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approve the sourcing-model and source-market decisions" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-595 (ensure controlled execution — Global Sourcing Strategy, Source-Market & Sourcing-Model Design (PA-122.1).)
- operational: consolidated category sourcing plan; operational: total-landed-cost framework (links to W3788)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fragmented-buying risk**: Each category/buyer imports independently with no enterprise leverage; mitigated by consolidated category sourcing plan
- **Margin-leakage risk**: Import landed cost not modeled end-to-end; mitigated by total-landed-cost framework (links to W3788)
System Touchpoints: - Merchandising (links to VS-01); supply planning (links to VS-02); finance/costing (links to VS-17.4/VS-106); freight (links to VS-110); strategy (links to VS-33)

steps.activity: Global Sourcing/Merchandising define the global sourcing strategy: which categories/SKUs to import vs source locally (informed by landed cost, lead time, quality, IP, volume), the import category sourcing plan per category (steel/cement/lumber, tiles, electrical, paint/coatings, power tools, appliances, hardware), target source countries, and the make/buy/consolidation approach, aligned to the merchandise financial plan (links to VS-101) and assortment (links to VS-01.1)

Global Sourcing/Finance model the import business case per category: FOB cost, freight, duty, brokerage, inland, financing (LC cost), shrink/damage, and overhead against local-source alternatives; confirm the import landed-cost advantage and margin contribution (links to VS-106 commodity, VS-110 freight)

VP Merchandising/Executive ratify the global sourcing strategy, approve the sourcing-model and source-market decisions (links to W3786/W3787), and cascade import sourcing targets to buyers/category managers

fields.Participants: Global Sourcing, Merchandising (links to VS-01), Supply Planning (links to VS-02), Compliance (links to VS-87/VS-86), Quality (links to VS-31), Risk (links to VS-21.2), Finance (links to VS-17.4)

workflows.name: Source-Market & Country Strategy, Geographic Risk Diversification

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "country strategy per category" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "Global Sourcing/Compliance screen all current and prospective source countries/vendors" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: concentration limits and alternate sources; operational: screening (links to VS-86)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Concentration risk**: Over-reliance on one country/vendor; mitigated by concentration limits and alternate sources
- **Sanctions exposure risk**: Sourcing from a restricted party/country; mitigated by screening (links to VS-86)
System Touchpoints: - Compliance/customs (links to VS-87); AML/sanctions (links to VS-86); supply risk (links to VS-02.3); treasury/FX (links to VS-18); risk (links to VS-21.2)

steps.activity: Global Sourcing define the source-market and country strategy per category: country capability/cost/quality/lead-time assessment, concentration limits (avoid over-reliance on a single country/vendor), and alternate-source qualification (e.g., Vietnam/India alternates to China for tools/hardware) — informed by trade-compliance and sanctions screening (links to W3792/VS-86)

Global Sourcing/Risk assess and manage geographic/country risk: tariff/trade-policy exposure (links to VS-87), geopolitical and shipping-lane risk (links to VS-02.3/VS-69), currency exposure (links to VS-18), and concentration risk; define diversification thresholds and a fallback sourcing map

Global Sourcing/Compliance screen all current and prospective source countries/vendors for sanctions, restricted-party, and trade-policy exposure (links to VS-86/VS-87), and maintain the approved-country/vendor-source list

fields.Participants: Global Sourcing, Merchandising (links to VS-01), Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-34), Finance (links to VS-17.4), Legal (links to VS-100.3), Quality (links to VS-31), Compliance (links to VS-22)

workflows.name: Sourcing-Model Decision: Direct vs Sourcing Agent vs Overseas Buying Office

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-model of "evaluate and decide the sourcing model per category/vendor" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "performance review" scorecard vs thresholds (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-595 (ensure controlled execution — Global Sourcing Strategy, Source-Market & Sourcing-Model Design (PA-122.1).)
- operational: model-decision framework; operational: governance and direct audits (links to W3796)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Model-mismatch risk**: Direct buying without capability, or agent over-reliance; mitigated by model-decision framework
- **Agent-capture risk**: Sourcing agent controls vendor/price information; mitigated by governance and direct audits (links to W3796)
System Touchpoints: - Legal/contracts (links to VS-100.3/W688); vendor master (links to VS-03); finance (links to VS-17.4); ABC (links to VS-86.3); data privacy (links to VS-91); governance (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: Global Sourcing/Strategy evaluate and decide the sourcing model per category/vendor: (a) **direct** import (BuildRight buys ex-works/FOB from the factory — highest control, lowest unit cost, highest overhead); (b) **sourcing agent** (a third-party agent sources, consolidates, and manages vendors on BuildRight's behalf — links to W3793); (c) **overseas buying office** (BuildRight's own staff/office in the source country — links to W3794); based on volume, complexity, control, cost, and capability

Global Sourcing/Legal structure the chosen model contractually: direct supply agreement, sourcing-agent agreement (scope, commission, exclusivity, IP, anti-bribery links to VS-86.3, data links to VS-91), or overseas-office establishment/legal-entity (links to VS-100/VS-36); define KPIs and governance

Global Sourcing/Finance publish a periodic sourcing-model ROI review (unit cost, overhead, quality, control, risk by model) and recommend model migration (e.g., agent → direct as volume grows) to governance (links to W3808)

fields.Participants: Global Sourcing, Logistics Finance (links to VS-17.4), Freight (links to VS-110), Customs (links to VS-87), Treasury (links to VS-18), Merchandising (links to VS-01), Commodity (links to VS-106)

workflows.name: Total-Landed-Cost Sourcing Framework, Incoterms & Payment-Terms Strategy

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Logistics-Finance maintain the total-landed-cost" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "Global Sourcing/Legal define the Incoterms strategy" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-route of "routes and recommend the lowest-TLC sourcing that meets quality/lead-time/risk…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-595 (ensure controlled execution — Global Sourcing Strategy, Source-Market & Sourcing-Model Design (PA-122.1).)
- operational: TLC framework; operational: payment-terms strategy (links to VS-105)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Hidden-cost risk**: Sourcing on FOB price alone ignores freight/duty/financing; mitigated by TLC framework
- **Cash-flow risk**: Aggressive LC terms strain working capital; mitigated by payment-terms strategy (links to VS-105)
System Touchpoints: - Freight (links to VS-110); customs/tariff (links to VS-87); treasury/LC (links to VS-18/VS-105); commodity (links to VS-106); finance/costing (links to VS-17.4); legal (links to VS-100.3)

steps.activity: Global Sourcing/Logistics-Finance maintain the total-landed-cost (TLC) framework and calculator: FOB/ex-works unit cost, ocean freight & surcharges (BAF/CAF), duty/tariff (links to VS-87), brokerage, insurance, inland, port/handling, LC/financing cost (links to VS-18), shrink/damage allowance, and overhead → landed cost per unit and per SKU, by source/vendor/route

Global Sourcing/Legal define the Incoterms strategy (FOB, EXW, CIF, DDP) and payment-terms strategy (LC at sight, usance LC, TT, open account, CAD) per source/vendor/category, balancing cost, control, risk, and cash flow (links to VS-18/VS-105); negotiate into contracts

Global Sourcing/Finance compare landed cost across sources/vendors/routes and recommend the lowest-TLC sourcing that meets quality/lead-time/risk constraints (links to W3807), tracking actual vs planned landed cost

fields.Participants: Global Sourcing, Private Label (links to VS-41), Merchandising (links to VS-01), Quality (links to VS-31), Design/R&D, Legal/IP (links to VS-100.2), Compliance (links to VS-117)
fields.Trigger: Private-label strategy (links to VS-41); OEM/import-vendor development

workflows.name: Import Sourcing Make-to-Order, OEM & Private-Label Linkage

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-import of "import OEM/private-label vendors" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "performance review" scorecard vs thresholds (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-595 (ensure controlled execution — Global Sourcing Strategy, Source-Market & Sourcing-Model Design (PA-122.1).)
- operational: IP agreements and audits (links to VS-100.2); operational: ongoing monitoring (links to W1838)
Pain Points / Risks: - **IP-leak risk**: OEM vendor copies BuildRight design/brand; mitigated by IP agreements and audits (links to VS-100.2)
- **Quality-drift risk**: Import OEM quality degrades over time; mitigated by ongoing monitoring (links to W1838)
System Touchpoints: - Private label (links to VS-41); quality (links to VS-31); IP/legal (links to VS-100.2); certification (links to VS-117); finance (links to VS-17.4)

steps.activity: Global Sourcing/Private-Label identify and qualify import OEM/private-label vendors: factory capability audit (links to VS-31/W160), sample evaluation, IP/contract-manufacturing terms and BuildRight-owned tooling/brand protection (links to VS-100.2), and certification (links to VS-117 DTI-BPS)

Global Sourcing/Private-Label develop the OEM/import vendor: specification, quality standard (links to VS-41.2/W1838), lead time, MOQ, and pricing (TLC links to W3788); integrate into the import sourcing plan (links to W3785) and product-development lifecycle (links to VS-41.1)

Global Sourcing/Quality/IP govern the OEM relationship: ongoing production quality monitoring (links to W1838), factory social-compliance audit (links to W1845/W1546), IP/brand protection (links to VS-100.2), and performance review (links to W3797)

workflows.name: Global Sourcing Risk, Resilience & Alternate-Source Strategy

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "country concentration, port/shipping-lane disruption" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-import of "Global Sourcing develop and maintain alternate-source and dual-source plans" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-route of "reroute, and accelerate/expedite per the resilience plan" (replaces manual Step 3).
Pain Points / Risks: - **Single-source risk**: Critical import SKU from one vendor/country; mitigated by dual-source
- **Disruption-unprepared risk**: No alternate when a source fails; mitigated by resilience plan
System Touchpoints: - Supply risk (links to VS-02.3); risk (links to VS-21.2); BCP (links to VS-26); treasury (links to VS-18); commodity (links to VS-106); quality (links to VS-31)

steps.activity: Global Sourcing/Risk maintain the import-sourcing risk register and resilience strategy: vendor/country concentration, port/shipping-lane disruption (links to VS-69 typhoon), tariff/trade-policy change (links to VS-87), currency (links to VS-18), commodity (links to VS-106), quality (links to VS-31), and supplier financial/ESG risk

Global Sourcing develop and maintain alternate-source and dual-source plans for critical import categories/SKUs (qualify alternates — links to W3786), safety-stock policy for import risk (links to VS-02), and pre-negotiated surge/fallback capacity

Global Sourcing/BCP run disruption-response sourcing activation (links to VS-02.3/VS-26): on event, activate alternate sources, reroute, and accelerate/expedite per the resilience plan; capture lessons

workflows.name: Trade Compliance & Sourcing Linkage (Tariff, Country, Sanctions)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Global Sourcing/Customs embed trade compliance into sourcing decisions" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-route of "route restricted sourcing" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - operational: compliance-informed sourcing; operational: screening (links to VS-86)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Duty-suboptimization risk**: Sourcing ignores PTA/FTA duty savings; mitigated by compliance-informed sourcing
- **Sanctions-violation risk**: Sourcing from restricted party; mitigated by screening (links to VS-86)
System Touchpoints: - Customs/tariff (links to VS-87); AML/sanctions (links to VS-86); legal (links to VS-100.3); finance (links to VS-17.4); analytics (links to VS-28.1)

steps.activity: Global Sourcing/Customs embed trade compliance into sourcing decisions: HS/HTS classification and duty impact per source country (links to VS-87), preferential-trade-agreement (PTA/FTA — e.g., ASEAN, ASEAN-China) utilization, anti-dumping/countervailing exposure, and country-of-origin rules — so sourcing is optimized for landed cost *after* duty

Global Sourcing/AML screen all import vendors/agents/countries against sanctions and restricted-party lists (links to VS-86), manage trade-policy and sanctions monitoring, and block/re-route restricted sourcing
Global Sourcing/Customs publish trade-compliance-informed sourcing analytics (duty saved via PTA/FTA, anti-dumping exposure, sanctions screening coverage) to governance (links to W3808/VS-87)
